newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus charges, releases Greenpeace activists.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus charges, releases Greenpeace activists.

text.p: Eight Greenpeace activists walked free in Cyprus on Friday after spending the night in jail for blocking the entrance to a government building during a protest in the capital Nicosia on Thursday.

The five men and three women, all foreigners, were charged on five counts ranging from vagrancy, blocking public access to a government building and causing a disturbance for chaining themselves to the gates of the ministry of agriculture and resources.

Wearing white boiler suits with "Greenpeace" emblazoned over the front, all eight denied charges read out by police prosecutors before a judge at the Nicosia district court. The court ordered their release on a 200 pound ($394) bond each, setting a hearing into the case on September 3.
Activists from the United States, Greece, Italy and the Netherlands were taken to court handcuffed, smiling broadly and doing the "V" for victory sign with their fingers.
All eight were among crew members of the Sirius, the Greenpeace boat now touring the Mediterranean. The Sirius is due in Lebanon on Saturday.
Greenpeace and local environment groups have been urging the authorities for years to turn the Akamas peninsula, an important turtle nesting site, into a protected zone.
But their move was strongly criticised by agriculture minister Costas Petrides, who said that blocking access to a government building was an affront to the state.
"A non-governmental organisation, whatever it may be, cannot visit a country and give the impression it does not respect the state which is offering it hospitality," Petrides told Cyprus radio.
"Closing the ministry and its entrance was disrespect to the state," he added.
Greenpeace campaigner Mario Damato said the group had not expected its activists to be put in prison overnight.
